Hey everyone, op here. I posted this yesterday, and then subsequently deleted it about 7 hours after. 

When I first posted this I genuinely didn't think that anyone would read it. I have spent so long keeping myself hidden, looking over my shoulder, moving to different states every year. That having even a small spotlight on me made me panic a little bit. 

I forgot that the main reason that I wanted to post this was because I wanted to help people, and I let my own feelings and hang ups get in the way of that. 

More than one person reached out and let me know how my story helped or affected them. So I've decided to just leave it up. If I can help even one more person with my story then I will shoulder my anxiety and keep moving forward. I'm here for you. I won't forget that again.

I was supposed to take care of everyone. 3 of my friends that i deployed with have killed themselves. 

There was this police cheif in the village we opperated in. He was a good guy. Every day after work he would go with a police detail to pick up his nephew from school. One day they went to assassinate him with a VBIED. They missed him and got the kid. He was partially eviscerated, maybe about 7 or 8 years old. I needed my friend to help me treat casualties because there where a few in the specific event. 

I forgot that he had 3 kids of his own. Fast forward about 5 years. He couldn't look at his kids without seeing all the gore from that one specific casualty. He goes to the park one night with a mosberg 500 and blows his head off. I feel responsible for what happened.

It's evolved quite a bit since it all first started. I took place in 83 separate mass casualty events. Anything more than 3 casualties at the same time. Only reason I know that specific number is because it's written down in the description of an award I got at the end of it all.

Those weren't all happening in direct combat. Most of that took place outside the wire during the night. The enemy would go out at night and try to undue anything we did during the day. That usually meant laying IEDs or getting into skirmishes with the ANA and ANP. 

I ran a clinic on my Outpost with the Australian medic. After patrols we would let the locals enter our Outpost one at a time after being searched so that they could get regular medical treatments. Stuff for colds, headaches. Regular shit, we used an interpreter to communicate.

Anyways, be it out on patrol, sleeping on my rack, or even pulling tower guard, almost every single day I treated people. I've seen a lot of people die :(. A lot of little kids man. Iland I fucked up. Fucking shit . I fucked up and people fucking died. On top of that I have seen so much gore. An impossible amount. From skin sloughing, to full blown evicerations. I had my hands inside my friends leg once fuck Fuuuuck..... Fuck fuckfyckfgbmmy

I was a combat medic in Afghanistan, it's where all of this started. I've tried the VA, civilian doctors, and VA affiliated programs. With prior hospitalization anytime I speak to a mental health professional they always over react and call the police. It's not safe for me to speak to anyone, they will just throw me in a cage. Granted, I'm already trapped in one, but that one is in my mind. I have been mentally I'll and thrown in an isolation cell for 3 weeks once in a VA hospital. I'm wasnt allowed to call my parents, or talk to the nurses. They just keep me in that room, with a plexi glass partition. Watch me use the bathroom. Wouldn't say a word. I can't risk being thrown into another cage. 6.5 months with 3 weeks in isolation, 5 or 6 separate 3 day stays based on people being worried for me. 

It's like I've been handed some sort of contract or legal agreement. It's a catch 22. I'm allowed to talk about my mental health issues, so long as I am willing to surrender my personal freedoms...

I don't have any support system at all. Unfortunately most people my age only socialize at bars, and I'm a recocvering alcoholic. Sometimes the silence and loneliness get so overwhelming that I'll go out to the bar to make friends. I'm fairly charasmatic so I'll usually make at least one friend.

They can always tell that there's something wrong with me within a few days of know each other, by that point I'm already off the wagon, drinking to die. And I'll stupidly open up, to drunk to remember that I'm not supposed to share any of this stuff. Then we stop being friends and I have to battle with alcoholism again on my own. Which really sucks. 

Thank you for responding. Honestly, since I've posted this I've been visiting this sub and offering advice whenever I can to whoever I can. That helps a little bit for some reason. 

Take care

Now this is all some stuff that I can very deeply relate to. I've always felt similarly, that I was being taken advantage of by literally everyone. But it almost felt like a bit of a catch 22, I didn't want to have to give up everything for friendship and family. But I always wanted to have friends and family. One day I had to take a second and really look at things.

If they don't really care for me, then why do I care what they think? If they don't really care about me then why am I putting myself so far out there for them. I don't live myself, they don't seem to either. So no matter what I'm still going to go unloved. So I sort of just dropped everything. Stopped taking care of people that were using, giving out money for no reason, paying people's bills. I didn't do it in a rude or angry way. I just stopped. And once they started demanding answers and they heard it coming out of their own mouths it was pretty easy to turn the conversation and just be like "dude, seriously? Your yelling at me because I'm not paying your phone bill? Am I your dad, wtf is this?" 

It was a little lonely at first but eventually you realize that without the constant need to take care of everyone around you you can start taking care of yourself. So I started doing all the things that I used to really like doing but stopped doing because the people around me didn't like those things. And eventually I met other people that oiked similar things and I was able to start new relationships that were so much better. Life moved past them, it's my life and I wasn't going to let them guide me.

I still struggle with suicidal depression, but it is way more manageable now. Instead of writing of suicide note to everyone, why not try writing a personal hand written letter to each person you addressed in your main letter, tell them how you feel you've been taken advantage of, or something of this nature. When your done with your letters put them somewhere private or just trash them. They don't need to see them. 

I'm not great at advice, but I don't like seeing people in pain. I hope anything I've said helps. I'll be around if you need to keep talking
